cards.title: One census kernel: a fight runner with read-only observers and one report harness
shared_surfaces: committed evidence digests under docs/change-requests/evidence/ (read as pins, never rewritten)
acceptance: case 1: for every rival build x seeds censusSeedStart..+7, the kit-based runBuildFight(seed,id) -> deep-equals a fixture captured from the pre-refactor runner at 2d83a1e (hash, casts, answers, cleanHits, exchanges, distanceByBucket) - the fixture is written first, so the test fails until the kit exists and passes only if nothing moved

cards.body:
## Summary
The census scripts share one shape - build a Games, step it to an end, watch events, map phase to outcome, digest seed:hash, summarise, validate args, write an evidence envelope - and every census re-types all of it. Extract `census-kit.ts`: `censusFight({seed, wave, composition, options, prepare?, observers, maxSeconds})` where observers are read-only `{step(g, newEvents), finish(g)}`, plus `fightDigest`, one `median/quantileSummary`, `parseCensusArgs`, `evidenceEnvelope/writeEvidence`. The builds instrumentation, the coverage watchers and the named dead-air/ledger readings become observers; the week arms become `prepare`.

## Description
Today a new arm or a new reading means forking the loop: runWeekBuildFight's armed branch (week-census.ts:94-101) forks createGames and the loop and silently drops every builds-census reading. counter-coverage re-does the build setup. Five outcome mappings, six digest sites, five medians with two empty-set policies, four arg parsers. The kit makes the loop one function and the readings composable, so `--arm lag` build cells can carry casts and hits/exchange (the short-duel reading D1 6.8 names as next) and any future census is an observer, not a fork.

## Flow
- Capture a fixture of today's runBuildFight / coverageBuildFight / runNamedFight / runWeekFight outputs on 8 seeds per cell (before any change).
- Write census-kit.ts + census-kit.test.ts (cases 5-7) and the fixture parity test (case 1) - red.
- Port builds-census, counter-coverage, named-census, week-census onto censusFight with observers; port the five writers onto parseCensusArgs/writeEvidence. report-w2/w3/w4/ladder stay (legacy evidence dirs).
- Green: fixture parity, committed digests (case 2 and the existing week-census.test.ts:58 d1-weeks pin), then `npm run gate`.

## Expected impact
One loop instead of six; armed build fights gain the full builds reading; a new census reading is ~20 lines of observer. Simulation untouched: observers only read, the hashes are the proof.

## Evaluation
Claim: the census scripts run on one kernel with no change to any fight hash or committed digest.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (census-kit.ts does not exist; armed week build fights return 5 fields).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - census-kit.test.ts + fixture parity + existing builds/named/counters/week tests + `npm run gate`; digests checked against d1-exchange-after.json and d1-weeks.json.
Result: better
Gate: architecture
cards.evidence: grep of the loop: builds-census.ts:34, counter-coverage.ts:81, named-census.ts:18, week-census.ts:89, week-census.ts:99, report-ladder.ts:13. Armed return at week-census.ts:100: `return { seed, build: buildId, outcome: outcome(g), durationS: ..., hash: stateHash(g.state) };` vs runBuildFight's 20+ fields at builds-census.ts:61-65. d1-exchange-after.json summaries fire_close digest dd746f4e (node probe), also the week-1 fire_close build digest in d1-weeks.json and d1-weeks-arm-lag.json (same dd746f4e) - the kit's parity anchor is already in the repo.

cards.title: census:compare - two evidence files in, the D1 before/after table out, with noise verdicts
shared_surfaces: packages/core/package.json scripts block (one added line: census:compare)
acceptance: case 1: compare(d1-exchange-before.json, d1-exchange-after.json) -> 6 rows keyed by build; fire_close medianS 15.8 -> 67.0 with band verdict 'out -> in' against [45,75]; markdown row contains '15.8 -> 67.0' and '47.0% -> 49.5%'
case 2: compare(d1-weeks.json, d1-weeks-arm-lag.json) -> every one of the 20 week-1 wave/build rows (both profiles) has verdict 'same' (digests equal); no week-1 row reports a delta
case 3: air_close win rate 0.525 -> 0.400 at n=200 -> verdict 'moved' (two-proportion |z| ~2.5 > 1.96); fire_light 0.455 -> 0.505 at n=200 -> verdict 'noise' (|z| ~1.0)

case 4: air_close after = 0.400 against winRateTarget [0.4, 0.65] -> range verdict 'in, on edge' because its 95% Wilson interval [0.335, 0.469] straddles the 0.40 floor (the doc's 'that is the reading, not a margin', computed)
case 5: compare(a builds-census file, a week-sweep file) -> throws 'different census kinds: builds vs weeks'
case 6: two files with different seedRange or count -> a header warning 'seed ranges differ: digest equality not meaningful' and no row is ever 'same'

case 7: compare(docs/waves/W8-evidence/named.json, docs/change-requests/evidence/d1-named-after.json) -> wave 3 row Brennic median 16.5 -> 63.0 s (durationS.p50), win 55.2% -> 44.6%, 'moved'; the named shape (waves[]) is read through the same adapter as builds (summaries[]), counters (cells[]) and weeks (cells[].waves/builds)

docs/concepts/D1-combat-followup-and-progression.md:144-145 - 'air_close sits exactly on the 40% floor; that is the reading, not a margin' and 'The far builds hold within the 200-seed noise' - noise judged by eye, no interval anywhere in scripts/

packages/core/scripts/report-builds.ts:27 / report-weeks.ts:23 / report-counters.ts:31 / report-named.ts:22 - every writer already stores a per-cell digest, fights and winRate, so the comparison data exists and is never read back

packages/core/scripts/report-builds.ts:2 - `--exchange off` is documented as 'the before arm', and report-weeks.ts:2 offers --arm level|ranked|lag: the reports are designed for A/B, but nothing compares A to B
packages/core/package.json:17-21 - census:named/builds/weeks/counters/skills writers exist; no reader or compare script
docs/change-requests/evidence/ - 34 tracked evidence files, most of them arms of one another (d1-exchange-before/after, d1-rank-*-4/5, d1-counters-*-off/held/bank, d1-weeks-arm-*)
cards.rollback: Single additive commit: three new files and one package.json script line. Revert deletes them; no runner, writer, evidence file or simulator file changes.
cards.runner_up: Band verdicts on the live report lines (each builds/weeks line flags out-of-band median and out-of-range win rate in the console, using the summary fields medianInBand/winRateInRange it already computes but never prints).
cards.body:
## Summary
The operator runs every census as an A/B - exchange on/off, rank 4/5, counters arms, week arms - and then compares the two JSON files by hand, transcribing D1's tables and judging 'same', 'noise' and 'on the floor' by eye. Add `npm --prefix packages/core run census:compare -- <a.json> <b.json> [--md]`: it reads any two evidence files of one census kind, aligns cells, and prints the before -> after table with a per-row verdict.

## Description
`census-compare.ts` (pure, IO-free like the other census modules): `loadCells(json)` adapts the four committed shapes (builds `summaries[]`, weeks `cells[].waves/builds`, counters `cells[]`, named `waves[]`) to flat cells {key, fights, winRate, medianS, digest, targetDurationS, winRateTarget}; `compareCells(a,b)` gives per row: digest-equal 'same', else a two-proportion z-test 'moved' or 'noise' on win rate, a Wilson 95% interval, band verdicts for median and win range with crossing ('out -> in') and 'on edge' when the interval straddles a bound; `renderTable` emits the D1 markdown table. `report-compare.ts` is the thin reader/printer. Refuses mixed kinds; warns on mismatched seed ranges.

## Flow
- Write census-compare.test.ts over the committed evidence files (cases 1-7) - red.
- Build the adapter, the comparator (Wilson + two-proportion z, no dependencies) and the renderer.
- Add report-compare.ts and the census:compare script; `npm run gate`.

## Expected impact
A D1-style reading goes from transcribing tables out of two JSON files to one command whose output pastes into the doc; 'within noise' and 'on the floor' become computed verdicts rather than prose judgement; digest-equal cells are found automatically. Pure reader: no fight is run, no hash can move.

## Evaluation
Claim: one command reproduces D1 6.1's before/after table from the committed files and labels each row same/noise/moved with band verdicts.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no compare module exists).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - census-compare.test.ts over committed docs/change-requests/evidence and docs/waves/W8-evidence files + `npm run gate`.
Result: better
Gate: direction
